metadata.description: Editorial chronology scaffolding for the Millennial Week timeline: the 7 thousand-year 'days' (2 Peter 3:8), the competing creation epochs, externally-anchored history, and prophetic milestones. Hand-authored from this repo's own studies -- not machine-generated like docs/data/genealogy/generated/*.json.

epochs.name: Genealogical epoch (Ussher/MT convention)
epochs.note: Zadok year 0 = 4004 BC. Shared by all four genealogy chronology variants in docs/data/genealogy/index.json's timeline_variants -- they differ in AM-distance to the Flood and to Terah, not in this creation-year anchor itself.

epochs.name: Millennial-week epoch (day-is-near.md)
epochs.note: Backed out from day-is-near.md's claim that AM 6000 = 2075 AD. Implies creation at roughly 3925 BC, about 79 years later than the genealogical epoch above -- an unreconciled discrepancy this site's own studies flag rather than paper over (see day-is-near.md and prophecy-events-times.md's 'Pivoting backward from the anchors').

anchors.label: Battle of Qarqar (Ahab)
anchors.evidence: Kurkh Monolith (Shalmaneser III), synchronized via the Assyrian Eponym Canon's Bur-Sagale eclipse (763 BC)

anchors.label: Sennacherib's invasion of Judah (Hezekiah)
anchors.evidence: Sennacherib's Prism (Taylor Prism) and the Lachish reliefs, British Museum

anchors.label: Jehoiachin's release (Evil-Merodach)
anchors.evidence: Jehoiachin's Ration Tablets (Weidner tablets), excavated Babylon

anchors.label: Cyrus's decree
anchors.evidence: Cyrus Cylinder; fall of Babylon dated by the Nabonidus Chronicle (539 BC)

anchors.label: Artaxerxes I's decree to Nehemiah
anchors.evidence: Elephantine papyri fix Artaxerxes I's regnal years independently

anchors.label: Merneptah Stele ("Israel" in Canaan)
anchors.evidence: Earliest extra-biblical mention of Israel as a people in Canaan -- a terminus ante quem for the conquest, not a date for the Exodus itself

milestones.label: The Exodus (early-date view)
milestones.note: 1 Kings 6:1's 480 years before Solomon's 4th year, pivoted from Thiele's Qarqar-anchored ~966 BC. Not itself an anchor -- a late-date Exodus in the 1200s BC is also held in scholarship.

milestones.label: Solomon's temple foundation (4th year)
milestones.note: Thiele's Qarqar-anchored reconstruction; roughly 46 years earlier than Ussher's unanchored 1012 BC for the same event.

milestones.label: Daniel's 70 weeks terminus (Anderson)
milestones.note: Sir Robert Anderson's 173,880-day count from Artaxerxes' decree (445 BC) lands 10 Nisan, 6 April AD 32 -- days before the Triumphal Entry.

milestones.label: Daniel's 70 weeks terminus (Hoehner)
milestones.note: Harold Hoehner's reworked count lands 10 Nisan, 30 March AD 33, corrected so the crucifixion falls on a Friday Passover.

milestones.label: The Crucifixion
milestones.note: AD 30, 32, and 33 all have advocates; this site's flagship calculation favors AD 33 (Hoehner) for weekday consistency with a Friday Passover.

milestones.label: Lunar eclipse over Jerusalem at Passover
milestones.note: Humphreys & Waddington (Nature, 1983): the only Passover lunar eclipse visible from Jerusalem in an eleven-year window, AD 26-36 -- a hard astronomical fact independent of how vivid it looked (contested by Schaefer, 1990).

milestones.label: Year 6000
milestones.note: The close of Day 6 / the threshold of the millennial Day 7, per day-is-near.md's reading of 2 Peter 3:8. Lands in a different Gregorian year on every epoch/variant rail -- that spread is the point of this timeline.

milestones.label: Millennial reign begins
milestones.note: The start of Day 7 (Rev 20:2-7) -- Satan bound, the thousand-year reign begins.
